| # Decisions log. 2026-10-28: written up as ADR 0111 (proposed) with a reference service (`src/sample-service/`), a service kit and a CI check that builds each service image and checks health, JSON logs, clean shutdown and config errors |

Status key: Decided (Didi confirmed), Proposed (written down, needs Didi's confirmation), Open (needs a decision, with who decides).

Dates are the day Didi decided. "By Oct 27" means decided in the planning sessions before Oct 28.

## 1. Decided

### Decided by Oct 27, 2026

| ID    | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D-001 | Windmill is the runner. Linear is a mirror, and our own state store is the source of truth                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| D-002 | Two machines: Machine 1 (idea) and Machine 2 (work item). Machine 3 (daily scan) comes later and feeds Machine 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| D-003 | A deterministic runner owns every transition. Agents never move themselves. Every state has one owner role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| D-004 | Bots are shared across all projects. Agents a bot dispatches are scoped to one project. The Council is shared. Expect 6 to 10 projects                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| D-005 | Escalation goes to the Council first, then to Didi only if the Council cannot resolve it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D-006 | Gates: approve-once (new secrets or permissions, dropping data, DNS changes each approved separately, PII access), only-Didi (spending money, personal messages and emails, production deploys, playbook rule changes), and visual approval for design. Free to run: job applications and forms, code, docs, staging deploys, internal tickets |
| D-007 | Production deploys in v1: Didi reviews staging each morning and approves the deploy on GitHub from their phone                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| D-008 | Scope: any new feature, new or changed user flow, or changed product direction goes to Didi. The Council decides priority, tech and architecture, naming and branding, and user-facing copy unless it changes approved direction                                                                                                               |
| D-009 | Done means: tests pass and CI green, matches the approved design (UI), docs updated or no docs impact stated, works on staging checked by a bot. Playbook proposals never block Done                                                                                                                                                           |
| D-010 | Nothing sits idle. If nothing blocks an item, the runner dispatches it immediately. Continue by default                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| D-011 | Spend alerts at a threshold and work keeps going. A looping item stops and goes to the Council. No daily cap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D-012 | The attention list is a table in the state store in v1. Channels only render it. A frontend comes later and the system builds it                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| D-013 | The state store is a relational database with node and edge tables. A graph database is not required                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| D-014 | Every new idea starts with an Interview of Didi (one question at a time, answers verbatim with the time) before any planning or building                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D-015 | Build order: dogfood. The first project through the system is the system itself                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| P-18 | Protected set: the system may never change these without Didi: the gate list and its enforcement code, the guards that authorize transitions and the privileged-path list, the runner's credentials and how they are issued, the metrics and the evaluation harness, spend caps and the kill switch, the rule that production deploys are Didi's, and this list itself. The proposer, the evaluator and the deployer are different roles, and the evaluator is a different model family. One improvement is in flight at a time, and every change is small and reversible. Success is judged on several outcomes (cycle time, failures, QA rounds, spend) with a held-out slice. QA strictness and thresholds are in the protected set: the system may propose changes to them, and only Didi approves them (D-153). A model never grades its own change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `docs/architecture/technical-architecture.md` section 2.13                                    |

A failed task or start ends the run `fail`; a refused or failed record cancels the run and ends it `cancelled`; if the cancel fails, the handle is kept for the cancel pass. Reason: a move written before `start` cannot be undone (transitions are append-only), and a started run can be cancelled |

| O-19 | How the approval page offers D-200's three answers, and what a timeout records **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.2 dispatch slice 2).** | A required `answer` field (Approve, Reject, Changes requested) and the required `reply` field from M0.4, so `approval_recorded` always has Didi's words. The checks sit on the item for now, since no project field holds them; a project default can be added when Triage fills items (M3.6). Reason: the smallest shape that holds what D-213 asks for |
| O-21 | How the Messages API loop sets the tier on its requests and which errors count as a Flex capacity rejection (ADR 0114 sections 8 and 9) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.2 dispatch slice 3).** | The loop adds `service_tier` to a request only when the route asked for Flex or Priority. A Standard request is sent exactly as before, because Anthropic, the only provider routed to today, does not take `standard` as a value, and Standard is every provider's default. A Flex capacity rejection is a 429 whose error type, or message, names `engine_overloaded` or `overloaded_error`; DeepInfra's queue-timeout form is added once the rehearsal reads it. A capacity wait that would reach the run's minute limit is not started: the run ends on the rejection, so it is recorded `usage_exhausted` with cause `capacity` and queues, instead of being stopped by its deadline as `timeout`. Reason: the smallest change that keeps today's requests unchanged and lets the runner tell capacity from a deadline |
| O-22 | What `onCapacity: "next_candidate"` does with the usage-exhausted wait, and which candidate "ran" (ADR 0114 section 5) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.2 dispatch slice 3).** | When a later candidate passes the hard rules, the next dispatch takes it at once, without `usage_exhausted_wait_minutes`: the wait is for capacity on the candidate that was busy, and the point of the setting is not to wait for it. The candidate that ran is the policy entry with the same provider, model and tier as the item's latest run, read from that run's route columns. If the policy no longer lists it, no later candidate can be named and D-221 applies. Only a capacity end on the same task type counts; a rate limit or an out-of-credit end waits as today. The route's decision record says what happened (`afterCapacity`). Reason: deterministic from the store's records (D-162), and a policy change cannot send the item to a candidate before the one that ran |
| O-23 | Where and how an agent run's report asks for its contract move (ADR 0102, ADR 0107) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.2 dispatch slice 3).** | In the run-end flow, right after the end is recorded, through `src/core/run-reports.ts`: a `success` end asks the library for the moves out of the node's state that its role owns, for its track, leaving out escalations, the prose fallbacks, the dispatch move and the moves on which the runner merges (guard `qa_verdict_independent_on_head`). Each goes through `requestTransitionOnce` with trigger `bot_report` and id `run:<run id>`, so the guards decide from runner evidence and a retried flow moves once. A node that moved since the run started, other than by the run's own dispatch move, asks for nothing. A rejected move writes nothing and the item stays; the counter half of the fallback is M3.5. A run-end flow run again for an ended run asks again, so a done report whose CI was still pending moves once CI is green. A QA pass moves nothing until the merge is built (M3.3, D-218). Since M3.3 a QA pass goes through the merge (O-31). Reason: the end is the runner's own record of the run, the move must come after it, and the contracts already say which moves a report triggers, so no flow carries its own copy |
| O-24 | What the egress proxy counts as a rejected request, and what the run records as its reported cost (ADR 0114 sections 2 and 9) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.2 dispatch slice 3).** | Every upstream 429 counts as rejected, Flex or not, since none is billed; past `max_rejected_model_requests` every model request of the run gets 403 with its own fixed message, which maps to `budget_exceeded` with detail `proxy_rejected_ceiling`. `reported_cost_usd` is the runtime's own cost figure, the same value `cost_usd` holds until the core prices runs from the catalog; `first_token_ms` stays null, since neither runtime streams its requests. Reason: the proxy never reads bodies, so it cannot tell a Flex overload from a rate limit, and the ceiling exists to stop a runtime that retries without end |
| O-25 | Where a run's price comes from, so the runtime's dollar limit and the core's `cost_usd` both use the model catalog and a recorded run is always priced the same way (ADR 0114 sections 2 and 5, D-162) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.2 pricing slice).** | The core copies the route's catalog entry (the tiers the provider supports for the model and every tier's price) onto the run when it admits it, in the same transaction, as the nullable jsonb column `runs.model_price` (migration 0008), and never changes it. `recordEnd` prices the run from that copy, and the runner passes the same copy to the agent in `FOREMAN_MODEL_PRICE`, from which the Messages API loop prices each request; `src/agent-images/claude-api/pricing.ts` is removed. A run with no usable copy is not started (`buildKubernetesTask` and `checkRunSpec` refuse it, and the image refuses to start), and if one ends, its `cost_usd` stays null rather than its end being refused. The image's model id rule also takes DeepInfra ids with one `/` (for example `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-Turbo`). Reason: reading the catalog again at the end, by `model_catalog_version` from `settings_log`, would depend on every price change bumping the version and on the log being kept forever; a copy on the row is exact, needs no history, and the core reads only the run. The column is nullable so the migration needs no empty table and no made-up values |
| O-26 | How `cost_usd` prices a `mixed` or unknown served tier, a tier with no catalog price, and cache writes with no listed price (ADR 0114 section 8, docs/costs.md section 2) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.2 pricing slice).** | `mixed` and null (no response reported a tier) are priced at Standard, as ADR 0114 section 8 already says; a reported tier the provider does not support for the model is priced at Standard, which is what it is billed at. A supported tier with no catalog price (hard rule 2 checks only the requested tier and Standard) is priced at the highest cost any of the model's prices gives. A cache write is priced at the tier's `cacheWrite`, or at its uncached input rate when the catalog lists none, as on DeepInfra. The Messages API loop prices each response by the same rules, so its limit and the recorded cost agree for a single-tier run. The catalog has no long-prompt rate card, so Claude Haiku 5.5's higher rate above 100,000 prompt tokens is not modelled; Haiku is not in the catalog, and adding it needs that field first. Reason: each rule prices at least what the provider can bill for those tokens, except a Priority request with no reported tier, which ADR 0114 still prices at Standard (Priority is chosen only when Didi names it). The task brief suggested the requested tier for a null served tier; the accepted ADR says Standard, so the ADR was followed |
| O-27 | The OpenCode model's `limit` values (OpenCode 1.19.5 needs both `context` and `output`) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (OpenCode image).** | `limit.output` comes from `FOREMAN_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, falling back to 16,000 as in the Messages API image, since OpenCode reads 0 as 32,000, above DeepInfra's cap of 16,384. `limit.context` is 0, which OpenCode reads as unknown and which turns its automatic compaction off: the model catalog has no context size per model yet. A long run then ends on the provider's context error or on its limits instead of being summarised. Reason: no made-up context sizes, and compaction requests were not exercised in the spike. Revisit when the catalog gains a context size |
| O-28 | How the OpenCode wrapper prices steps for its cap, when it stops OpenCode, and what it reports about capacity and the served tier (D-223) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (OpenCode image).** | Each step is priced at Standard, or at Priority when the route asked for Priority and the provider supports it; OpenCode's cost table gets the same prices. OpenCode reports no served tier, and Flex never bills above Standard. After each `step_finish` that is not the final answer, the wrapper stops when the cost plus the last step's cost reaches the cap (the spike's rule) or the turns reach the limit: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10 seconds, inside the pod's grace period. A run that ends on a retryable Flex capacity rejection reports `capacityRetries` 5, OpenCode's fixed retry count; the waits are not reported, and no other run reports capacity. The served tier is read from a step if OpenCode ever reports one; 1.19.5 does not, so the proxy's figure stands (ADR 0114 section 8). Reason: the cap never counts a step below what it can cost, and the result claims only what the events show |
| O-29 | How a run's provider tells the OpenCode image its API and address, and how migration 0009 changes the rejected-request ceiling (D-222, D-223) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (OpenCode image).** | `ModelProviderSetting` gains an optional `api: { kind, path }` (`anthropic` with `/v1`; `openai-compatible` with `/v1/openai` for DeepInfra). The agent Job gets `FOREMAN_MODEL_API` and `FOREMAN_MODEL_BASE_URL` (`<proxy>/<provider name><path>`); `baseUrlEnv` stays for the Claude Code fallback. `checkRunSpec` refuses a bad kind or path, more than one provider with an API, and a Developer or Designer run whose provider has none. Migration 0009 sets `max_rejected_model_requests` to 6 where it is below 6 and leaves a higher value alone. The wrapper refuses `.opencode`, `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc` in its working folder or any folder above it, not only at the root. Reason: one place per run for the API, a fail-closed check before anything starts, and a migration that only raises the ceiling to what OpenCode needs |
| O-30 | How the merge guard checks "not past the round cap" (build plan M3.3, FR-7) without counting a round twice **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.3).** | A new guard `qa_rounds_below_cap` on both merging moves: `qa_round < qa_round_cap`. `not_third_failed_round` is not reused: it runs on the fail move before that round is counted, so it adds one (`qa_round + 1 < cap`), and on a pass it would refuse an item whose second round failed. The merge counts no round. At the cap the item belongs to the Council (`escalation_trigger_met`), whose resolution resets the counter (P-03). ADR 0105's guard list and the registry test now hold 26 names. Reason: the cap is checked once, by the count the counter already keeps |
| O-31 | The merge's order of writes and how a failure after the merge is recovered, since a merge on GitHub cannot be undone and transitions are append-only (M3.3, like O-17) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.3).** | `src/core/merge.ts`. Check the move's guards; read the PR and record its mergeable state (`merge_check`, a fact, also in dry run); check again; on a privileged-path failure alone open the gate request and wait; otherwise squash-merge with GitHub's `sha` set to the head the guards checked, so a later commit is refused. Nothing but the `merge_check` is written before GitHub merges, and a refused merge writes nothing else. After the merge: the `merge_commit` under GitHub ingestion's ingest key (`github:merge_commit:<repo>#<pr>`), then the move with that key as its trigger id (kind `event`). Recovery: every later call (the run-end flow again, or the reconcile flow's merge pass, which runs in live mode because the live pass is not built) finds the PR merged and does only the last step, and only when the merged head is the node's head; a PR merged at another head is reported `merged_at_another_head` and left to a person. The key and the trigger id keep the evidence and the move to one row each. In dry run nothing is merged and the move is a dry-run row under the caller's trigger. Reason: the irreversible step comes before anything that claims it happened, and everything after it is idempotent |
| O-32 | What evidence the no-conflict guard reads (D-218) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.3).** | A new evidence kind `merge_check`, `{pr, mergeable: true \| false \| null}` on the head commit, written by the runner right before it merges from GitHub's `mergeable` for the head GitHub reports (nothing is recorded when that head is not the node's head). `no_merge_conflict_on_head` passes only on `true` for the current head and fails closed on `false`, `null`, a check for another commit, or none. Migration 0010 adds the kind and requires its commit. A base branch that moves after the check is caught by GitHub refusing the merge, and by a fresh check on the next attempt. Reason: the guard reads only what the runner read itself (essential 6, D-162), and GitHub ingestion does not need a new event |
| O-33 | When the merge opens a privileged-path gate request, and what it holds (M3.3, D-102) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.3).** | Only when `privileged_paths_approved` is the only failing guard after the mergeable check, and not in dry run: kind `privileged_path`, owner `didi`, blocking, topic `privileged-path:<nodeId>`, payload `{commitSha, repo, pr, paths}`. Asking again for the same head keeps the open request; a new head opens a new one, which supersedes the old (schema invariant 5). The approval page's answer copies `kind: "privileged_path"` and the request's `commitSha` into the decision's scope (`src/core/approvals.ts`), which is what the guard reads; a request without a full commit sha gives an approval that matches no head. Reason: Didi is asked once per head, and only when their approval is what stands between QA's pass and the merge |
| O-34 | How the runner learns that main has deployed an item's merge commit to staging (build plan M3.4), since no staging deploy signal was defined and ADR 0113 records `deployment_status` as a delivery only **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.4).** | A project's deploy on push to main reports to GitHub as a deployment to the environment named `staging` (GitHub Actions does this for a job with `environment: staging`). The runner asks GitHub for the deployments of exactly the node's latest merge commit to `staging` (`listDeployments(repo, environment, sha)` on the GitHub adapter) and records one whose latest status is `success` as `staging_deploy` evidence, `{environment, deploymentId}` on the merge commit, under `github:staging_deploy:<repo>:deployment-<id>`. A deploy of the head or of any other commit records nothing, and `inactive` (staging moved on) does not count. Event path: the `verify_staging` flow, called with the repository and commit of a `deployment_status` event, verifies only the item whose latest merge commit is that commit, and reads the deploy from GitHub again rather than from the event. Who calls it on the event is open, like the other called flows: the receiver holds no Windmill credential, and giving it one is a new credential. Backstop: the reconcile pass (dry run) and the reconcile flow's staging pass (live). The receiver and `factory_ingest` are unchanged, so no role gains a permission. Migration 0011 adds the kind and lets the runner key it. Reason: ADR 0113 says a deployment is not evidence by itself and only tells the runner to run its own check; reading the deploy itself keeps essential 6 and needs no wider role. Extended by D-225 and O-38: a deploy of a later commit that contains the merge commit counts, and a failed one is recorded |
| O-35 | Who runs the staging check, and how its result is recorded (build plan M3.4, ADR 0107, essential 6) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.4).** | The runner, as plain code, not a QA agent run: ADR 0107 ("the QA model reads; plain code checks") and the contract's `tools` for Verifying on staging ("checked by plain code the runner runs") settle it. The core defines a `StagingChecker` port (`check({project, commitSha})` returning `pass` or `fail` with the commit staging serves, or `no_result`); the deploy adapter implements it (ADR 0111, M3.7), and until then the composition's checker refuses, so nothing is recorded. A result counts only when staging serves the merge commit. It is recorded as `staging_check {pass}` on the merge commit by the runner, once per merge commit under `runner:staging_check:<repo>@<sha>`, in live mode only. A thrown check records nothing and is tried again. Reason: no new bot, and the guard reads only evidence the runner produced itself |
| O-36 | How the contract's timeout for the staging move ("The QA bot's budget (not set). Re-dispatch once, then the Council") applies to a check that ends without a result (M3.4) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.4).** | A check that could not reach staging, ran out of its own time limit, or found staging serving another commit records `staging_no_result {reason, attempt}` on the merge commit, keyed per attempt and per entry into the state. The next call re-dispatches the check once. After the second, the runner asks for Escalated to Council with trigger kind `timeout`, and `escalation_trigger_met` now also passes on two such rows on the latest merge commit in the current state (`STAGING_CHECK_ATTEMPTS`, from the contract's words). A no-result does not count toward `failure`. The time limit itself is the checker's, since the budget is not set. Reason: the attempts are store records, so the retry and the escalation are decided from them (D-162), and the existing escalation move carries it |
| O-37 | The order of writes after a staging check, and how a failure part way is recovered (M3.4, P-03, like O-31) **Decided 2026-10-31 by the implementing agent (M3.4).** | Pass: the move to Done with the counters reset in the same transaction (`requestTransitionOnce` now takes writes that commit with the move, as `requestTransitionWith` does), then the release of each item the Done item blocks (trigger `done:<node id>`, the guards decide). Fail: the fallback move back to In development or Building components with `failure` up by one in the same transaction, then the escalation, which the guards allow at `failure_threshold`. The item escalates from the building state, so the Council's `return` sends it back there; the fail move has no guard against the third failure, unlike QA's fail move. Both moves have trigger `staging_check:<check evidence id>`, so a repeated call writes one row and counts once. Recovery: the reconcile flow's staging pass asks again for the escalation of an item whose last applied move was a staging fail, and for the release of every Done item's dependents. Dry run writes a dry-run row for a check already recorded, and no counter. The Spec section on a design item's developer item at Done is not built (left for the design handoff). The switches note stays where the text has it, the second line, at the top of the page. **Escaping:** every piece is escaped as HTML text (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`), recorded text after the same JSON quoting the text uses, so nothing from the store (titles, names, reasons, questions, Didi's words, plan lines, the Council's reasons, scan titles, guard notes, bot output) can add markup or leave an attribute. The page is only `div`, `section`, `h2` to `h4`, `p`, `ul`, `li` and `a`, with inline `style` (system font, 16px, a narrow column that wraps long ids, no fixed colors so it reads in light and dark mode); no script, no external resource, no image and no form. **Links, only two kinds:** (a) a project's recorded staging address when it parses as an absolute `https:` URL with no user name or password, as its normalized form, escaped as an attribute, with `rel="noreferrer"`; `http:` is not linked, since nothing in the codebase checks the recorded address's scheme and `https:` is the narrower rule. Any other address is shown as text. (b) The Windmill page of a flow the caller names (`flowPages`), only as a plainly relative path on Windmill's own origin (one leading slash, then letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.` and `/`, no `..`, no query), behind Windmill's sign-in, never a public or signed-token link (D-295). The flow names one: `f/foreman/hold_release_request` at `/scripts/get/f/foreman/hold_release_request` (`HOLD_RELEASE_REQUEST_PAGE`, `flows/lib/held-items.ts`), Windmill's page for a script at that path, since `flows/windmill.yaml` pushes each entry as a script. Beside each link the text still says the address, or the flow's path and its input with the item id, so the page works if links cannot be tapped. **Shown ids:** as the text (O-91): item ids, and the gate request id of each of Didi's questions; no approval link, topic key, decision, run, project or evidence id, no secret and no personal data beyond what the text shows. A test checks the page shows exactly the ids the text shows. No reopen is offered (D-314). **Not changed:** the generator and its content, the 06:00 America/Toronto schedule (D-297), the 24-hour window (D-298), reads only, runs whatever the switches say. Nothing is sent: no push alert, no email, no new account, credential, resource or store read. **Tests:** `test/daily-check-render.test.ts` (unit: escaping of `<script>` and `"><img onerror>` payloads in every field, both link rules, the same sections and order as the text, no other id, an empty check and an empty project, the switches note), `test/flows/daily-check-flow.test.ts` (the result's shape, the held item's link). No DB test: no new store read. **To verify at rehearsal** (first-hosting runbook, "Reading the daily check"; Windmill's docs page "Rich display rendering" says only that an `html` key renders as HTML and `render_all` renders several views): (1) the address of the flow's run list to bookmark, latest run first; (2) that a result with only `render_all` shows the page and then the JSON; (3) whether Windmill sanitizes the HTML and what it strips; (4) whether links can be tapped and where they open; (5) whether the relative link resolves to the Windmill origin and opens the right page signed in, whether it needs `?workspace=<id>`, and whether the page is `/scripts/get/...` or `/flows/get/...` once deployed; (6) whether the page can prefill the item id (not relied on); (7) that it reads well on Didi's phone, light and dark. Reason: D-319 and D-320, built from what the check already says, with the narrowest links that do the job and every recorded value treated as untrusted. |
| O-101 | How the state API and the GitHub receiver start their flows through one Windmill proxy (D-283, D-284, D-291, D-327 to D-329) **Decided 2026-11-05 by the implementing agent (event-driven slice 1 of 4).** | **The proxy (D-284, D-328):** `windmill-proxy` in `foreman-platform` (`infra/kubernetes/platform.ts`), one Deployment, one ClusterIP Service on 8080 and one NetworkPolicy, running the agents' egress proxy image (`images.egressProxy`, the same digest as `proxyImage`) with the manifest conventions (one replica, limits, read-only root file system, non-root user, `/health` probes, no service account token). It is configured only from the environment: `ALLOWED_HOSTS` is `windmill.host` alone, `MODEL_PROVIDERS` `[]`, `STATE_API_UPSTREAM` empty, and no Secret. Three settings the proxy requires have no meaning here, so they take the QA fetch proxy's values for a proxy that serves no model traffic (`MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS` and `MAX_REJECTED_MODEL_REQUESTS` 1), and `RUN_ID` is the fixed log label `windmill-proxy`: the proxy's code is unchanged. Policies: the state API and the receiver keep DNS and the database port and gain only TCP 8080 to the proxy's pods, with no 443; the proxy accepts only those two pods on 8080 and reaches only DNS and TCP 443 on public IPv4. Policies match addresses, so the proxy's allow-list is what holds the calls to the host; it resolves the name itself, refuses private addresses and never decrypts the tunnel. `windmill.host` and `windmill.workspace` are plain manifest settings, checked by the same parsers the services use; both services get `WINDMILL_HOST`, `WINDMILL_WORKSPACE` and `HTTPS_PROXY` (the proxy's Service address). **The call (`src/adapters/windmill/client.ts`):** one small client that starts a script by path without waiting for it: a CONNECT tunnel to `<host>:443` on the proxy in `HTTPS_PROXY` (its own few lines, as the OpenCode wrapper's GitHub client does, not Node's environment proxy, so nothing else in a service is routed through it), TLS inside it with the system's certificate authorities and the host as server name, then `POST /api/w/<workspace>/jobs/run/p/<path>` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and the JSON arguments. The script form `run/p/` because `flows/windmill.yaml` pushes each entry as a script; the endpoint is one constant, `RUN_BY_PATH_ENDPOINT`. Each entry's `main(input)` takes one argument named `input`, so the body is `{"input": {"ideaId": ...}}` or `{"input": {"nodeId": ...}}` (`entryArgs`). It resolves on any 2xx and never reads the answer; the whole start is bounded at 5 seconds. A failure is `WindmillStartError` with the step (`tunnel` or `start`) and the status, never the token or a body; both services log only the error's type, step and status (`startErrorFields`). `NotBuiltError` is kept only for a missing token: the token is read by its secret path, trimmed, visible ASCII only, and null while unset or empty. The host, workspace and proxy are required plain settings, so a bad value stops the service at start and is named, never shown. Run scopes are `jobs:run:scripts:<path>` (`runScope`). **The state API (D-283):** `src/api/main.ts` builds `windmillPlanApprovalFlow(token, target)` from those settings, as O-84 left the port; a failed start still never fails `POST /plans`. The fake is now `src/adapters/windmill/fake-flow-start.ts`, shared by both ports. **The receiver (D-291, D-327):** the ingest result now names each PR head whose CI end the delivery newly recorded (`finishedCi`: a newly inserted final `ci_run`, success or failure, never pending), so a replay, a racing copy or the same fact from another delivery names none. Both conclusions count, because capture does not read the conclusion and a failed CI may still have rendered the bundle. For each such item, `src/github-receiver/flow-starts.ts` asks capture's own due check and starts `f/foreman/option_capture` only when it is due, before answering the webhook (as the state API awaits its start), with the start bounded so GitHub's 10 seconds hold. A failed check or start is logged with the delivery id and the error's fields only, never an item id, and changes neither the answer nor the evidence. The token's flow list is one constant, `RECEIVER_FLOW_PATHS` (today only option capture), at `platform/github-receiver/windmill-token`, Secret `github-receiver-windmill-token`, optional. The receiver now reads the contracts in its image (`contracts/machine-1`, `contracts/machine-2`) only for the states capture works in; it records no move and no spec version, and its image and the flows' bundle are built from the same commit at deploy. **The due check:** capture's first reads moved into `createCaptureReads` (`src/core/option-capture.ts`): the switches (read as every flow reads them), the item in a capture state, its latest Designer run ended `success`, and its PR head. `capture` itself now starts with them, and `due` adds only whether the head is captured, so the two cannot drift. Whether the head is captured is read from capture's own screenshots at the head (runner-recorded, ref `runner:option_screenshot:<head>:`), not from the request, since the receiver's role cannot read gate requests: capture writes both in one transaction, and a PR's head moves only to new commits, so the two agree. The one exception is a branch force-pushed back to a head already captured, which capture would capture again; the receiver then starts nothing and the reconcile pass captures. **Privileged change for Didi's review, migration 0020:** `factory_ingest` gets `select` on `factory.settings`, with a row policy that shows it only the `kill_switch` and `dry_run` rows; it still cannot write any setting or read `settings_log`. Needed because the receiver must not start a run under the switches (D-164) and nothing it could read held them; a column grant cannot help (the store reads whole rows), and copying the switches into its environment would be a second copy of the truth. No grant on gate requests is needed (the screenshots above). **Not changed:** the state API still starts the flow under the kill switch or dry run, as O-84 built (the flow then does nothing). **Tests:** `src/adapters/windmill/client.test.ts` (integration, the real egress proxy configured as the Windmill proxy and a local TLS fake Windmill: the path, method, bearer header, arguments, server name, the tunnel to the vetted address only, another host refused with 403 and nothing sent, an untrusted certificate refused, a refused start, an unreachable proxy and a timeout each naming step and status and never the token or the answer, a missing token refused with no call, the settings), `test/github-receiver-starts.test.ts` (over HTTP: due starts once; a replay, the same CI end from another delivery, a pending result, a captured head, a code item, a running Designer, the kill switch and dry run start nothing; a new head starts again; a failed start keeps the answer and the evidence and logs only the type), `test/option-capture.test.ts` (the due check agrees with capture: before and after a capture, after Didi's answer, a new head, each wait under capture's own name, a head with no bundle yet), `test/github-ingest.test.ts`, `src/api/planning.test.ts` (the real adapter as `main.ts` builds it: no token stays refused and calls nothing; with one, the start goes to the proxy for the Windmill host only), `test/db/github-ingest.test.ts` (migration 0020, and the due check as `factory_ingest`), `test/platform-manifests.test.ts` (the proxy's policies, its environment read by the proxy's own config reader, the services' settings read by their own reader, only the connector and the proxy reach 443), `test/flows/windmill-description.test.ts` (the receiver's secret and flows, and the runbook's scopes). **To verify at rehearsal** (first-hosting runbook, "Starting flows from the state API and the receiver"; Windmill's docs could not be fetched here, so this follows Windmill's docs as the coordinator read them on 2026-11-04): (1) that `POST /api/w/<workspace>/jobs/run/p/<path>` starts the script asynchronously, or that the entries are flows and the endpoint is `run/f/`; (2) that Windmill reads `export const main = (input) => ...` and the body `{"input": {...}}`; (3) that the run endpoint takes the bearer header; (4) that each token with only its `jobs:run:scripts:<path>` scopes starts its own script and is refused for any other script and any other call, and which status a refusal has; (5) the status of an accepted start (201 expected); (6) that the Windmill host resolves to public IPv4 addresses only, and that from both pods a direct call fails, the proxy's tunnel opens and another host is refused; (7) that a start finishes well inside 5 seconds; (8) that each start adds one run to the month's count and a replay adds none; (9) that the workspace id passes the manifest check. Reason: the smallest build that makes both starts event-driven with D-284's egress rule and D-328's one proxy, reuses the agents' proxy and capture's own check, and widens the receiver's role by two settings rows only. |
| O-102 | How the run watcher records each run's end when its Job stops (D-330, D-329 slice 2) **Decided 2026-11-05 by the implementing agent (event-driven slice 2 of 4).** | **The service (`src/run-watcher/`):** `main.ts`, `settings.ts` and `starts.ts`, a Dockerfile that installs no package (Node built-ins only) and `container-check.env`, with the service-kit conventions (configuration only from the environment, one JSON object per log line, `GET /health`, exit 0 on SIGTERM), in the CI container check and Dependabot like the other services. Settings: `PORT`, `KUBERNETES_API` (the manifest sets `https://kubernetes.default.svc`, the name the API server's certificate carries), `AGENT_NAMESPACES` (the rendered projects' `agents-<slug>` names, comma-separated, each checked; none is allowed), `WINDMILL_HOST`, `WINDMILL_WORKSPACE`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and the token at `platform/run-watcher/windmill-token`. No database setting, no package and no store import: it holds no database access. **The Kubernetes side (`src/adapters/agent-runtime/kubernetes/job-watch.ts`):** in the Kubernetes agent runtime adapter, where ADR 0106 keeps Kubernetes code; the service only composes it. Plain HTTPS with Node built-ins, sharing the runner client's request and error reading (`apiRequest`, `apiFailure`, `checkApiServer`, now exported from `client.ts`), so no new dependency. The token and the CA are read from the pod's mounted ServiceAccount files for every call, because the kubelet replaces the token before it expires; a missing or empty file fails the call as `NoCredentials`. Per agent namespace: list `batch/v1` Jobs with the selector `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=foreman-runner,foreman/component in (agent,fetch)`, then watch from the list's resourceVersion with `allowWatchBookmarks` and `timeoutSeconds=300`. When the server closes a watch, the next one resumes from the last version seen (bookmarks included), 1 second later. A 410, as an ERROR event or as the answer's status, lists again at once. A failed list, a failed watch or a dropped watch lists again after 1, 2, 5, 10, then every 30 seconds. One watch per namespace, because the Role is per namespace: a cluster-wide watch needs a ClusterRole. The namespaces are a setting because the watcher cannot list namespaces (D-330 grants Jobs only): `render.ts` passes the same project list it makes the namespaces and their Roles from (`platformObjects(settings, projects)`), so a new project is a re-render, which restarts the watcher, which then sends that namespace's stopped Jobs. **Which Jobs:** a run's agent Job and QA's fetch Job, the two Jobs `poll` reads. The fetch Job counts because its failure ends the run (`fetch_failed`) and its success is what moves QA to its review; without it both would wait for the backstop. That is one more run for each QA review run (D-164). Proxies and repo map Jobs are not a run's end and are skipped. The run id is the `foreman/run-id` label, taken only when `runNames(runId)` gives the Job's own name; the runner wrote both when it created the Job, and no agent holds a Kubernetes token. **Stopped:** `jobState`, moved into its own file `job-state.ts` (still exported from `result.ts`) so the watcher and `poll` read a stop the same way and the image needs no result parser: a `Complete` or `Failed` condition with status True. `SuccessCriteriaMet` or `FailureTarget` alone is not a stop yet (pods still stop). A passed `activeDeadlineSeconds` is `Failed` with `DeadlineExceeded`; a crash, an out of memory kill and a killed pod (deleted or evicted) are `Failed`, because `backoffLimit` is 0. A Job being deleted, or deleted before it stopped, sends nothing: that is the runner's own cancel, whose flow records `cancelled` and cleans up itself (sending would cost a run and race it), or a delete by hand, which the reconcile pass catches. **Once per process:** the starts keep every Job taken by namespace, name and uid, so a later event, a fresh list after a 410 or a drop, and a start given up are never sent again by the same process. A deleted Job's key is dropped (a uid never comes back); a key missed in a gap stays until a restart, a few bytes each. On startup the first list sends every stopped Job still present: the run-end flow's `cleanup` deletes the Job once the end is recorded, so these are the unrecorded ones, plus any whose cleanup failed, for which the flow answers `already_recorded` at the cost of one run. **Retries:** a failed start (any error but `NotBuiltError`) is tried again after 5, 30 and 120 seconds, four tries in all, then logged as not started and left to the reconcile pass. Each start runs on its own, so one waiting start holds up no other; on SIGTERM the waits stop and the Job, still present, is sent by the next process. A start that timed out after Windmill had accepted it may be sent once more; the flow records one end, at the cost of one run. A missing token is `NotBuiltError`: not retried, logged once per Job, and nothing reaches the proxy. Log lines name the namespace, the Job's kind (`agent` or `fetch`), how it stopped, the attempt and the client's step and status (`startErrorFields`), never the run id (a database id), the Job's name (which holds it), the token or Windmill's answer. A Job that stops before the dispatch flow has kept its handle gets `no_handle` and is not sent again; the backstop records it. **Cluster objects:** ServiceAccount `run-watcher` in `foreman-platform` with `automountServiceAccountToken: false`; only the watcher's pod sets `serviceAccountName: run-watcher` and `automountServiceAccountToken: true`, and every other platform pod still mounts no token. In each agent namespace, made by `agentNamespaceObjects` with that namespace's other standing objects, a Role `run-watcher` with exactly `batch` `jobs` `get`, `list` and `watch` (`RUN_WATCHER_ROLE_RULES`) and a RoleBinding to `run-watcher` in `foreman-platform`. No ClusterRole or ClusterRoleBinding, and no other permission was needed. The watcher's calls use list and watch; get is in the Role as D-330 names it. `PLATFORM_NAMESPACE` moved to `namespace.ts` so the binding and the platform objects share it. Deployment `run-watcher`: one replica on the platform pool with the same hardening as the other platform pods (non-root, read-only root file system, capabilities dropped, seccomp, limits from `resources.runWatcher`), `/health` probes, its image at `images.runWatcher`, and no Service. **NetworkPolicy `run-watcher`:** no ingress (the kubelet's probes come from the node, as the connector's do); egress to cluster DNS on UDP and TCP 53, to each `kubernetesApi.addresses` entry as a /32 on `kubernetesApi.port`, and to the Windmill proxy's pods on 8080, and nothing else. No existing policy reaches the API server (the runner calls it from Windmill Cloud), so this follows the platform policies' own pattern of a narrow ipBlock: a policy sees the address the `kubernetes` Service sends to, not the Service's, so the setting is the address and port of the `kubernetes` EndpointSlice in `default`, read at first hosting, step 7. Both are plain settings, checked as plain IPv4 addresses and a port other than 53. The `windmill-proxy` policy now accepts the watcher's pods as its third caller. The token's Secret `run-watcher-windmill-token` (key `token`) is optional, as in O-101. **Tests:** `src/adapters/agent-runtime/kubernetes/job-watch.test.ts` (unit: which Jobs are a stop, the run id rule, the settings, the mounted credentials read per call; integration, a local TLS fake API server, `fake-api-server.ts`: the list's path, selector, bearer token and CA, a refused list naming only status and reason, an untrusted certificate refused with nothing sent, the watch's query, events, bookmarks, a 410 both ways, a clean end, a drop and a stop; the loop: list then watch per namespace, resume without a list, list again after a 410 or a drop, a refused list waited on, deletions passed on), `test/run-watcher.test.ts` (in-process: each way a Job stops starts once, a running Job starts nothing, a 410 or a drop lists again without a second start, a restart starts only the stopped Jobs still present, a missing token starts nothing and reaches no proxy, a failed start is tried four times and then given up with no token in any log, a start that fails once starts once, no database access, and the process itself), `src/adapters/agent-runtime/kubernetes/namespace.test.ts` (the Role: only jobs, only get, list and watch, in the agent namespace, bound to the watcher's account), `test/platform-manifests.test.ts` (the account, the only token mount, no Service and no ingress, the egress rules, the proxy's third caller, the namespaces read by the watcher's own settings reader, bound only in agent namespaces, nothing cluster-wide), `src/adapters/windmill/client.test.ts` and `test/flows/windmill-description.test.ts` (the run-end start's path and input, the token's one scope, the runbook's line). **To verify at rehearsal:** the list in the first-hosting runbook, "Recording run ends with the run watcher", recorded here with the date. Reason: the smallest build that records every run's end on the event with exactly D-330's rights, reuses the runner's own reading of a stop, the Windmill client and the shared proxy, and spends at most one run per stopped Job in a process. |
| O-103 | How the reconcile pass acts in live mode, and how a ready item's first run starts on the move (D-274, D-329 slice 3) **Decided 2026-11-05 by the implementing agent (event-driven slice 3 of 4).** | **One plan (`src/core/reconcile.ts`):** the `live_mode_not_built` stop is gone. The pass reads the kill switch first, then `dry_run` as the library does (missing means dry run), and reports `mode` `dry_run` or `live`. In both modes it runs the GitHub polling backstop and plans steps 2 to 4 with the same code: release, dispatch and advance from evidence. In dry run it writes its dry-run rows as before. In live mode it writes no transition row: a move whose guards pass is reported `due` instead of `planned`, and a dispatch admission allows is `planned` with the run it would record, as in dry run. The merge, staging and cancel steps keep their dry-run halves in dry run only, since in live mode they would act and the flow's live passes already take them. The stall check and the clean-up candidates only report, in both modes (closing a request is the gate lifecycle, M4.1). The attention list is the same in both modes: a ready item older than one interval with no run is listed even when this pass now starts it, since the flow that made it ready, or the previous pass, should have started it. **The first-run check (`src/core/ready-runs.ts`):** one read-only check decides whether a node's first run is due: its state has the move guarded by `agent_ready_not_on_hold` for its track (Ready for dev, Ready for design exploration), the state's owner is an agent role, the node may be dispatched (not escalated, held, stale or not agent-ready), no run on it is active, the wait after `usage_exhausted` has passed, and the dispatch move's guards pass now. The dispatch step decides each node in a ready state with it, in both modes, and the flows ask it right after a move, so the pass and the flows cannot drift. Dry run's plan is unchanged. **Acting on the plan (`flows/lib/reconcile-steps.ts`):** with `dry_run` off the reconcile flow acts first, in section 2.5's order. Release: each `due` move through `library.requestTransition` with the pass's own trigger and actor (`reconcile`), so the guards decide again and a lost race retries from a fresh read; once applied, the item's first run starts at once. Dispatch: the first run of each ready node the plan admitted, through `startRun` (`flows/lib/start-run.ts`), so the kill switch, dry run, one active run per item, the Developer and cluster limits, admission and the route all apply and the start records the dispatch move; a node that left the planned state is not started (`state_changed`), and a first run the plan's admission refused is reported with its reason. The plan's other dispatches (a builder's fix round, a run resumed after `usage_exhausted`) stay with the passes that already start them live (the builder runs pass, the Council and Triage passes), so each has one path; the dry-run plan also plans a resume for a role that does not own the node's state, which nothing should act on. Advance: each `due` move guarded by `ci_green_on_head` into In QA review through the library the same way; once applied, QA's run starts through `startRun` with the plan's pull request and head commit (`qaHeadOf`), when the plan admitted it. Nothing throws on a refusal or a failed start: each is reported (`released`, `dispatched`, `advanced`, `firstRuns` in the flow's result) and the next trigger or pass tries again. **The order in live mode** (also in the header of `flows/lib/live-passes.ts`): the kill switch (then only the cancel pass), the polling backstop, release with the released item's first run, dispatch, advance with QA's run, merge, merged-change, staging with the first runs of the items a Done frees, escalation with the first run of an item returned to a ready state, follow-up, Council, redo with the first run of the item back at the start or its rework item, cancel, close, plan approval, Triage, hold release with the released item's first run, option capture, and last the builder runs. **First runs on the move (`flows/lib/ready-runs.ts`):** `startReadyRuns` asks the check for each given node and starts each due one through `startRun`, as `startBuilderRuns` does for fix rounds. It does nothing while the kill switch or dry run holds the runner (the pass takes the item on once both are off), adds no Windmill start or token, and reports only the nodes that were due. Every move that can make a node ready, and where its first run starts: (1) a release from Blocked by the pass: the reconcile flow, right after the move; (2) a release, or a design item in Ready for design exploration freed, when a blocker reaches Done: the staging flow and the live staging pass, for every item the Done node blocks (`firstRunsAfterStaging`); (3) the Triage handoff creating items: the run-end flow of the Triage run, for the idea's `split_into` items; (4) Didi's approval of a hold release: the approval resume step, and the live hold release pass; (5) a redo back to the start of a track, and a merged item's rework item: the redo pass, in the run-end flow of the Council's reversal run and in the live pass; (6) an escalation returned to a ready state: the run-end flow of the Council's run, the approval resume step after Didi's answer, and the live escalation pass; (7) a reversal answer clearing a ready item's stale flag, and a "still needed" answer that keeps a ready item: the run-end flow of the Council's run (the run's item and each cleared item); (8) Didi's answer to the request that was all that held a ready item (a Triage needsDidi request, say): the approval resume step, for the request's item, only when no switch holds the runner; (9) a move asked of the transition flow (`f/foreman/request_transition`), a release say: that flow, right after an applied move. No ready move happens outside a flow: the state API creates ideas, adds edges (which can only add a blocker) and records reports, and the GitHub receiver records `ci_run` and `merge_commit` only, and a blocker reaches Done only through the staging flow. Left to the pass: an item whose start was refused (a limit, no route) or failed, a Done or a release made by hand, and anything a flow cut short. **Defect fixed:** a Council run that ended `usage_exhausted` on a node that is not escalated (a "still needed", reversal, scanner or plan question) made the dispatch step ask for a Council dispatch with no question, which the dispatch refuses by throwing, so the whole pass stopped in dry run, and would have stopped every live pass. The step now leaves it to the Council pass, which runs a question again after the wait. **Windmill run budget (D-164):** the pass stays one Windmill run per schedule, whatever it starts, and an in-flow start runs inside the flow that took the move: neither calls the dispatch flow, so no Windmill run is added per item, and no new token or start is needed. The dispatch flow now has no automatic caller and stays for a start by hand. It then checks for plain IPv4 addresses and exactly one port, as before, and also applies the render's own rule for these values, which the real address no longer passes through: no `0.0.0.0`, and a port from 1 to 65535 that is not 53. Across all objects it finds the egress rules whose `to` is exactly one ipBlock `192.0.2.1/32` with `except: []` and whose only port is 443. It requires exactly one, gives it one `/32` ipBlock per address and the real port, and refuses if the placeholder still appears anywhere in the file afterwards. Each refusal is fixed text that holds no address, and leaves the file as it was. It prints only the number of addresses, and writes no job output, environment variable or summary. The file is changed in place on the runner and is never uploaded or printed; in `kubectl-apply`, the apply and `platform-checks.sh` use it. Not built: a diff in `kubectl-apply`, which has none. Each job reads the address itself, so if it changes between the plan and the apply, the apply uses the one it read. **The checks:** `platform-checks.sh` takes the probe's API targets from the run watcher's policy in the swapped file instead of `KUBERNETES_API`, and fails, naming no address, when that policy holds the placeholder or no address. **The credential:** `cluster-credential.sh`, after writing the kubeconfig, reads its `server` URL and refuses an empty one or one with a space or control character. The host name is exact, with no leading `*`, so a route matches no other host. Cloudflare's API reference "Create Worker Route" names `Workers Routes Write` and marks `script` optional, and the routes page lists "a Worker to invoke" among what a route needs and says a route with no Worker bypasses Workers; neither says whether a route may name a Worker that does not exist yet, or what Cloudflare serves until it does (read 2026-11-07). **The order:** the record and the route come in the plan of the add-a-project pull request, before the first staging upload (D-353) creates the Worker. The list reads no repository, and a token without `repositories` reaches every repository, so it names the one the runner already reads its settings from, for metadata only. The list is `GET` on the same path without the id, 100 a page ("Secrets" organization read). The restart is `POST /repos/didi-build/<slug>/actions/workflows/bootstrap.yml/dispatches` with exactly `{"ref":"main"}` ("Actions" write), done only on 204. PUT and DELETE go through a new port that follows no redirect (`src/adapters/github/write-http.ts`). Until the runner App exists every token port refuses with `NotBuiltError` (`flows/lib/compose.ts`). **The removal when Bootstrap ends:** the receiver already handles `workflow_run` (`HANDLED_EVENTS`), and GitHub lets an App subscribe to it with "Actions" read, which the runner App has (D-267, GitHub's webhook docs). A run started by a push is left alone: the form's grant can come while Bootstrap's first run, at creation, is still running, and removing the access when that run ends would leave the restart without it. The receiver's role cannot read projects, so the flow removes the access for any repository of the organization, which for one that is not a project is what the backstop does anyway; it does not read the run. Counted as no failure; the reconcile pass tries again" (`pendingDeployError`: the latest such row since the item entered its state while no deploy is recorded, and only the runner's fixed text). The builder's return reason gives the refused set's fixed text instead of a GitHub state. N-103 asks Didi how an infrastructure refusal should count. **The backstop:** in the reconcile flow's passes, before the staging pass (`flows/lib/live-passes.ts` step 4, `stagingDeploys` in the result): for each project with an item in Verifying on staging whose merge commit has no `staging_deploy` and no counted failure, the newest successful push run of CI on main (`GET /repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=main&event=push&status=success&exclude_pull_requests=true&per_page=1`) is deployed when its commit counts for one of them. That covers a missed event, an infrastructure refusal and an item that reached Verifying on staging after its build was deployed. A project with nothing waiting reads nothing. In dry run it reports `would_deploy`; under the kill switch it does not run. **The check** (`src/adapters/deploy/staging-checker.ts`, the `StagingChecker`, now composed for real since it needs no credential): `GET https://<slug>.didi.build/foreman-commit.txt` (`projectStagingUrl`), no redirect, no cache, 10 seconds, at most 1 KiB; 200 with exactly a commit, with or without its newline, is `pass` with that served commit, and the core requires a commit that contains the merge commit (D-225 rule 1, O-39); any other 200 body, such as the single-page fallback, is the new no-result reason `no_marker`; another status or no answer is `unreachable`; out of time `timed_out`. **The switches:** under the kill switch the receiver starts nothing, the flow refuses and the core reads nothing; in dry run the receiver starts nothing, and the flow and the backstop read the run and the compare and say what they would deploy and which items it would cover, fetching, uploading and recording nothing. **The credential:** one Cloudflare API token, account-owned, with only Workers Scripts: Edit on the account, a new credential behind Didi's gate (runbook step 16). It lives in Windmill resources only: `f/foreman/platform/cloudflare/staging-deploy-token` and `f/foreman/platform/cloudflare/account-id`, type `foreman_text`, value `{"content": ...}`, as O-110's, at the secret paths `platform/cloudflare/staging-deploy-token` and `platform/cloudflare/account-id`; the account id is kept as a secret as D-361 keeps it. `windmillStagingDeployCredentials(env)` reads both by path each time and never keeps or logs them; until the token exists the composition passes `unbuiltStagingDeployCredentials()`, which refuses with `NotBuiltError`, so each deploy is `credential_unavailable` and nothing reaches Cloudflare. The runner App gains no permission. **Retired** (O-104's staging start, D-356): the receiver's `deployment_status` start and its due check (`createStagingReads`, `ReportedDeploy`, `StagingDue`, the log lines `staging flow started` and `not started`), the ingest result's `deployment`, the flow `f/foreman/verify_staging` (`flows/verify-staging.ts`), its scope and `VerifyStagingFlow`, `verifyCommit`, GitHub's deployment reads (`GitHubDeploymentReader`, `Deployment`, `DeploymentState`, `listDeployments` and `listRecentDeployments` on the port, the adapter, the fake and the refusing clients), `STAGING_ENVIRONMENT`, `STAGING_DEPLOY_SCAN_LIMIT` and the `github:` deploy keys, each with its tests. A `deployment_status` delivery is still recorded. **Not built:** `health`, `logs` and `teardown`; the contract test across two targets; Launchpad's step. The `foreman` project has no route (O-112), so its staging Worker is uploaded but serves nowhere and its check gives no result until N-96 is settled. **Docs:** the runbook (the credentials paragraph, step 15's scopes and logs, "The receiver's starts on green CI and on CI's build on main", the staging route list, and the new step 16 with "The first staging deploy"), ADR 0111, ADR 0113's note, the architecture (sections 2.1, 2.5, 2.7 and the item lifecycle), `docs/guards.md`, the build plan's M3.4 note, `docs/test-plan.md` (item 26 and the event starts) and `flows/windmill.yaml`. **Tests:** listed in `docs/test-plan.md` item 26: `src/adapters/deploy/site-files.test.ts`, `cloudflare-staging.test.ts` and `staging-checker.test.ts`, `src/adapters/github/staging-builds.test.ts` (unit, fakes), `test/staging-deploy.test.ts` and the rewritten `test/staging.test.ts` (unit, memory store), `test/github-receiver-staging.test.ts` (in-process HTTP), `test/flows/deploy-staging-flows.test.ts` with the reconcile, builder run and live flow tests (flow, memory store), `test/preview-check-workflow.test.ts` (repo guard), and `test/db/staging.test.ts` (Postgres). Mutation checks by hand: breaking each new guard fails a test. **To verify at the first real run:** the runbook's "The first staging deploy" list (step 16), recorded here with the date: the artifact, Cloudflare accepting the SHA-256 hashes and the Worker with no module, the route serving, the marker, the staging check passing, a second push with no change, the refusals, and no route, domain or DNS change. | O-117 | How every connection to the database is encrypted and verified: one TLS builder, Supabase's CA in the repository, `sslmode` stripped, and a local opt-out (D-364) **Decided 2026-11-08 by the implementing agent (database TLS slice).** | **The builder:** `databasePoolConfig` in `src/adapters/store-postgres/tls.ts` gives the `pg` pool config of every production connection: the state API (`DATABASE_URL`, 10 connections) and the receiver (5) through `databaseSetting`, so a refusal stops the service at start and names the setting, never its value (ADR 0111); the runner's composition (`flows/lib/compose.ts`, 2), which throws the refusal; and `npm run db:migrate` (`MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`, 1). A connection that does not verify fails, and `pg` never retries it in plain text. **What Supabase's docs say about the session pooler (read 2026-11-08):** "Postgres SSL Enforcement" (supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/ssl-enforcement) recommends `verify-full` once enforcement is on, has the CA downloaded from the SSL Configuration section, connects with it to the shared pooler's host in its example (`aws-0-eu-central-1.pooler.supabase.com`, `sslmode=verify-full`), and says that for the shared pooler the setting governs both legs, client to pooler and pooler to Postgres. "Connecting with PSQL" (supabase.com/docs/guides/database/psql) connects to the Session pooler's host with `sslmode=verify-full` and `sslrootcert` set to the downloaded certificate. "Connect to your database" (supabase.com/docs/guides/database/connecting-to-postgres) says to verify with `sslmode=verify-full` and the root certificate from Database settings, and gives the session pooler as `aws-[INDEX]-[REGION].pooler.supabase.com:5432`. So, by the docs, the session pooler's certificate chains to the downloadable CA and matches its host name, and the host name check is on. No page says otherwise. Nothing was checked against the real pooler from here: that is the first real run's check. **`sslmode` in the connection string, stripped:** `pg` 8.23.1 merges the parsed string over the explicit config (`Object.assign({}, config, parse(config.connectionString))` in `lib/connection-parameters.js`), and pg-connection-string 2.14.1 sets `ssl` from `ssl`, `sslmode`, `sslcert`, `sslkey`, `sslrootcert` and `sslnegotiation`. So without the builder `sslmode=disable` gives plain text, `sslmode=no-verify` or `uselibpqcompat=true&sslmode=require` drops verification, any other `sslmode` replaces the CA with Node's own list, and `sslrootcert` reads a file the string names. The builder drops every query parameter whose decoded name starts with `ssl`, in any case, and `uselibpqcompat`, and keeps every other byte, so the password reaches `pg` as pasted. It then builds a `pg.Client` from the result, which opens no connection, and refuses unless `pg` keeps exactly the builder's TLS object, so a later `pg` that reads a new parameter is refused rather than weakened. Stripped rather than refused because Didi pastes the string exactly as Supabase's Connect panel gives it (runbook step 10), and stripping can only end in the strongest setting. **The certificate:** `src/adapters/store-postgres/supabase-ca.crt`, "Supabase Root 2021 CA" (O "Supabase Inc"), downloaded by Didi from the SSL Configuration panel and committed byte for byte on 2026-11-08: self-signed, CA:TRUE, key usage Certificate Sign and CRL Sign, valid from 2021-04-28 to 2031-04-26, SHA-256 fingerprint `80:70:25:AD:50:D4:ED:21:9D:2C:9C:7D:29:9C:00:4F:82:4E:B0:0C:F7:F6:5A:FE:F6:07:D0:7B:72:E6:CA:FA`. A test holds the file to that fingerprint and expiry. It must be replaced before 2031-04-26 (runbook step 10). It is not under `infra/`, which `.dockerignore` keeps out of every image build. `readDatabaseCa` refuses, with fixed text naming the path, a missing file or anything other than one or more PEM certificates that are each a CA (two are allowed for a switch to a new root). **Where it reaches each process:** the path is relative to the working directory, as the contracts are. The state API's and the receiver's images already copy `src/adapters/store-postgres` to `/app/src/adapters/store-postgres` and run from `/app`; a test holds both Dockerfiles to that and checks that `.dockerignore` keeps the file. The runner reads the contracts and bot files from its bundle by the same relative paths, so its bundle carries the certificate the same way: `flows/windmill.yaml` now lists `bundle_files` (`contracts/` and the certificate), the deploy step bundles them (runbook step 15), and `test/flows/windmill-description.test.ts` holds the list to the paths the code reads. There is no generated TypeScript copy. Without the file the runner refuses to connect, naming it. **The local opt-out:** `FOREMAN_LOCAL_DATABASE_WITHOUT_TLS=1` gives `ssl: false`, and only when the host `pg` will use (the URL's host, a `host` parameter, or `PGHOST` when the URL names none) is `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or a Unix socket directory. Any other host is refused, and so is any other value of the variable. Without it a local host still gets verified TLS. No deployment sets it: the rendered pods, the infrastructure code, the workflows, the Dockerfiles and `flows/windmill.yaml` are checked (`test/platform-manifests.test.ts`, `test/database-tls.test.ts`). It is named in `.env.example`. `test/db/` builds its own pools as before, and `test/db/tls.test.ts` reaches the local Postgres through the opt-out and is refused without it. **Follow-ups, not built here:** the migrations job (D-362, O-115, another slice) used psql with `PGSSLMODE=require`, which encrypts without verifying. Built in O-118 (2026-11-08): it now connects with `PGSSLMODE=verify-full` and `PGSSLROOTCERT` set to `src/adapters/store-postgres/supabase-ca.crt` in its checkout, and runs the runbook's plain-text check itself, sending no password. Each new check was broken once by hand, and a test failed each time. **To verify at the first real run:** the runbook's list "Database connections are encrypted and verified", recorded here with the date. Reason: one builder for every connection, with the strongest check Supabase documents for the session pooler, a certificate reviewed in the repository rather than fetched at run time, and no way for a pasted string or a variable to weaken it. |

| O-119 | Why the render leaves empty lists out of each NetworkPolicy it hands to `kubectl apply` (D-339, O-105) **Decided 2026-11-09 by the implementing agent (Platform plan fix).** | **Found:** Platform run 7 (started by hand to create the cluster's Secrets, right after run 6 applied the first objects) planned updates to three policies that nothing had changed, `cloudflared`, `default-deny` and `run-watcher`, so Didi had to approve an apply that changed nothing before the Secrets job could run. **Cause, reproduced:** against a local Kubernetes 1.33.0 API server and etcd (controller-runtime's envtest binaries), applying the real render server-side and then running the plan's own `kubectl diff --server-side` with `platform-diff.sh` listed exactly those three, every time. Each holds an empty list: no ingress rule (`ingress: []`, and for default deny `egress: []` too), and in the run watcher's API rule `ipBlock.except: []`. The API server stores an empty list as the field left out, but counts receiving `[]` for it as a change and raises the object's `metadata.generation` on every apply, which is the only line that differed. **The fix:** `forServerSideApply` in `infra/kubernetes/render.ts`, which the render command prints, drops every empty list from each NetworkPolicy's spec, at any depth, and touches nothing else. It means the same: each policy still names both `policyTypes`, so a left-out rule list still denies everything, and an absent `except` excepts nothing. The model in `platform.ts` and `namespace.ts` keeps its empty lists, which read plainly as "nothing allowed"; only the written form changes. Checked on the same local server: the fixed render, applied fresh or over what run 6 left, then diffed, lists nothing, an agent namespace's default deny included. Tests (`test/platform-manifests.test.ts`): no NetworkPolicy in the applied form holds an empty list, every one keeps both policy types, nothing else differs from the model, and the render command prints exactly this form; dropping the fix, or printing the model, fails them. The runner's own per-run policies are created, never planned or re-applied, so they are left as they are. **A slip, fixed the same day:** the first version of this fix (#106) broke the plan. `.github/scripts/api-server-address.sh` found the run watcher's placeholder rule by its exact shape, `except: []` included, so the plan job of the run its merge started stopped at "The rendered objects hold no egress rule to the API server's placeholder", before any diff; nothing was applied. Its tests had passed because they fed the script the model (`clusterObjects`) and not what the render command prints. The script now matches and writes the rule without `except`, and the tests' `renderedObjects` (`test/admin-workflows-fixture.ts`) is the printed form; with the old script, three of them fail with the plan job's error, and a swap that writes `except: []` again fails one. Checked end to end on the local server with the workflow's own scripts: render, address swap, plan (19 to create), apply, then a fresh render, swap and plan: "No changes"; and objects applied by the chain as it stood before #106, then planned by the new one: "No changes". **Effect:** a Platform run asks for the apply only when an object really changes, so a run started by hand for the Secrets asks once, for the Secrets. Reason: Didi approves at most the apply and the Secrets, and a plan that lists false changes would also hide a real one.
