Each holds the value itself, with no `{"content": ...}` wrapper. **A first run creates, a later one updates:** for each path the script asks `GET /api/w/<workspace>/variables/exists/<path>`, which answers `true` or `false`, then sends `POST /api/w/<workspace>/variables/create` with `{path, value, is_secret, description}` on `false`, or `POST /api/w/<workspace>/variables/update/<path>` with `{value, is_secret, description}` on `true`. This was chosen over "create, and on its 400 update" because telling that 400 apart from any other 400 means reading Windmill's error text, and the script never reads an answer that could repeat what was sent; `exists` answers with a fixed word. An update sends `is_secret` with the value, so a variable changed by hand goes back to its decided shape (Windmill refuses a change of `is_secret` without a value). **Kept from O-110:** values only through stdin or a private file, and the check's stdin is `/dev/null`; the Windmill token only in the header file; the log shows only `Created <path> in Windmill (HTTP status 201).` or `Updated <path> in Windmill (HTTP status 200).`; any status but 2xx, no answer, or a check answer other than `true` or `false` stops the run with fixed text and never shows the answer; the answer file is emptied before each check, so an earlier path's answer is never read again; the token and the endpoint are masked as before (D-349); nothing else is written. The Windmill token keeps D-352's secret name, `WINDMILL_RUNNER_RESOURCES_TOKEN`, so the workflow's job and its guard are unchanged: only the token's scope and value change. **Windmill's source** (version 1.865.0, a sparse clone of windmill-labs/windmill on GitHub, read 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-11): `windmill-store/src/variables.rs` (create checks `variables:write:<path>`, refuses an existing path with 400 "Variable <path> already exists" and answers 201; update checks the same scope, takes `value`, `is_secret` and `description`, answers 200, or 404 for a missing path; `exists` has no check of its own in the handler, and Windmill's route check (`windmill-api-auth/src/scopes.rs`, `check_route_access`) asks a scoped token only for a variables scope that covers reading, blind to paths (`variables:write` includes read), so the job's token can ask about any path and learns only whether it exists; a secret value is encrypted with the workspace's key on create and on update); `windmill-api-auth/src/scopes.rs` and `windmill-common/src/scopes.rs` (the route check ignores paths and a write scope includes read, so the token reaches `exists`, and listing variables shows only its paths); the migration `widen_variable_value` (a value of up to 15,000 characters, room for a PEM key). **The old resources:** `delete_resource` in `windmill-store/src/resources.rs` deletes a variable with a resource only when the resource's value names it as `$var:<path>`, which a `{"content": ...}` value never does, while `delete_variable` also deletes a resource at the same path. So runbook step 8 deletes the three old resources on the Resources page, not the Variables page, and explains the dialog's "linked" warning. The `resource_version` migration deletes a resource's history with it (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), so "Clear past versions" is not needed first; but `move_to_trash` keeps a deleted resource, value included, in the workspace's Trashbin for 3 days (the `trashbin` migration's default), so step 8 has Didi delete the three items there for good, check the three variables, and revoke the old `resources:write` token. This source keeps no history for variables, so an update leaves no older value readable. **Paths named here (decide during build):** D-368's "plain values beside" the keys are `f/foreman/platform/github/<role>-app-id` (`runner`, `developer`, `designer`, `qa`) and `f/foreman/platform/github/runner-app-installation-id`; the model keys are secret variables at `f/foreman/projects/<slug>/models/<provider>`. `flows/windmill.yaml` says every secret is a secret variable and every value a plain variable at `f/foreman/` followed by its path or name, gives the database login its `windmill_path`, and lists the Apps' four keys and five ids, each with its `windmill_path`, in a new `github_apps` list apart from what the composition reads, since no flow reads them yet (every GitHub token port refuses). **Docs:** runbook step 8 (the token's one scope `variables:write:` on the same three paths, Windmill's form Variables, Write and Restrict paths, the paste in place of the old token, the run, the old resources deleted with their Trashbin copies, the old token revoked), steps 12, 13, 15 (the database login, the four keys and the five ids, each path named) and 16 (the staging deploy token and the account id as secret variables), the secrets table and "The admin workflows"; the comments of `flows/lib/windmill.ts` (it still refuses every read), `flows/lib/environment.ts` and `src/service-kit/config.ts`; the Platform workflow's header comment; ADR 0106, ADR 0111, ADR 0103, the technical architecture and the test plan. `AGENTS.md` still says "Windmill resources" in three rules; it is not changed here, as its rules are Didi's. **Tests:** `test/admin-workflow-scripts.test.ts` (integration; the fake curl now keeps the variables and, as Windmill does, refuses a create of an existing path and an update of a missing one): a first run checks then creates, with the exact URLs, headers and bodies and only the token secret; a second run checks then updates; a variable changed by hand is put back into shape; the log shows only paths and statuses; the masks come first; no value reaches an argument or the check's stdin; a status of 302, 400, 401, 403, 404 or 500 on the check or on the write, no answer, and a check answer other than `true` or `false` are refused, showing none of the answer, and so is an empty answer after an earlier one. `test/admin-workflows.test.ts` (unit): the script's paths equal the yaml's, with the token under `secrets` and the other two under `values`, written as `true`, `false`, `false`; no resource route, type or shape is left; runbook step 8's scope is exactly `variables:write:` on the script's three paths, the secrets table names the same scope, and `resources:write` appears only where step 8 revokes it; the check reads `/dev/null`. `test/flows/windmill-description.test.ts` (unit): the database login's path; steps 15 and 16 store secret variables; the Apps' keys and ids, each path named in step 15, read by no flow. Mutation checks by hand, each failing a test and then restored: the token written as plain, or the CA certificate as secret; always creating; an update without `is_secret`; the value wrapped as `{content}` again; any check answer taken as `true`; the check's stdin left open; the answer file not emptied first; the check's status not checked; the check's answer shown in its refusal; the token's mask removed; the Windmill token in a header argument; runbook step 8's scope back to `resources:write:` or widened with `f/foreman/*`; the endpoint moved under `secrets`; an App key's path changed; the database login's `windmill_path` removed. **UNCONFIRMED, to check at the next run and record here with the date:** that the hosted Windmill runs code that matches this source; that its form makes a token with exactly `variables:write` on the three paths and that the path limit holds as the source says; that deleting the resources takes their history and leaves the variables, and that the Trashbin holds them until they are deleted there; whether curl writes an output file for an empty answer (the script empties the file first, so either way is safe). Reason: D-370 with the smallest change to the job, the same properties as O-110, and no credential but the Windmill token D-370 names, which Didi makes. |
| O-122 | Why Dependabot's auto-merge tries again when the base branch moved **Decided 2026-11-11 by the implementing agent (auto-merge fix).** | **Found:** of eleven Dependabot PRs opened together on 2026-11-11, eight merged on their own and three (#114, #117, #119) stayed open, green and labelled. Their auto-merge jobs failed with GitHub's "Base branch was modified. Review and try the merge again. (mergePullRequest)": another PR had merged a moment before, and `scripts/dependabot-automerge.mjs` stopped at any refusal other than the clean-status one. Nothing triggers the job again for a PR whose CI already passed, so such a PR waits for a person. **The fix:** `mergeDependabotPr` tries again after 15, 30 and 60 seconds on that one refusal only (`isBaseModifiedError`), each time asking for auto-merge first and merging at once when GitHub says the PR is already mergeable, as before; any other refusal still fails the job at once. Nothing else changes: which PRs qualify (minor and patch, the label, Dependabot's branch) stays as it was. Tests (`test/dependabot-automerge.test.ts`) drive it with a fake `gh`: one try, the clean-status path, a retry that succeeds, giving up after the last wait, and no wait on other refusals; removing the retry fails two of them. The script comes from the Launchpad template, so the same change goes to Launchpad with the other ports. |
